title: Unbound Local
statement: Implement `solve(assigns, read_before)`. Both strings are `yes` or `no`. `assigns` is `yes` when the function assigns to the name anywhere in its body. `read_before` is `yes` when the read happens before that assignment. Return `error` when the name is assigned anywhere and the read happens before the assignment (UnboundLocalError). Return `local` when the name is assigned and the read happens after the assignment. Return `global` when the function never assigns the name.
constraints: Any assignment in the function makes the name local for the whole function
hints: If the function never assigns, the read is global.
If it assigns and the read is first, the result is error.
If it assigns and the read is after, the result is local.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Python decides that a name is local if any assignment to it exists in the function, including an assignment that has not run yet.

editorial: Python decides that a name is local if any assignment to it exists in the function, including an assignment that has not run yet. A read of that name before the assignment raises UnboundLocalError instead of falling through to the global. No assignment at all means the read uses the global.
